explanation: The execution is faulty because upstream provenance ranks were assigned in ascending demand_score order instead of preserving demand-descending provenance order. Those incorrect ranks were handed off exactly to job_2, and job_2 correctly used the supplied upstream_rank ordering when ranking unsupported needs first. This made n06-r07 rank ahead of n06-r01 even though n06-r01 has the highest demand_score.
cited_evidence: Behavioural criteria require preserving deterministic source provenance identities, weights, and demand-descending rank order.
Top-level input demand order is n06-r01 score 9, n06-r02 score 8, n06-r03 score 7, n06-r04/n06-r05 score 6, n06-r06 score 5, n06-r07 score 4, n06-r08 score 3.
Job-2 input evidence_sources shows reversed/ascending ranks: rank 1 n06-r08, rank 2 n06-r07, ..., rank 8 n06-r01.

Upstream function assemble_provenance source sorts with sorted(rows, key=lambda record: (record.get('demand_score', 0), record.get('record_id', ''))), which is ascending rather than demand-descending.
Handoffs for needs and evidence_sources have matching producer_sha256 and consumer_sha256, so job_2 received the upstream artifacts exactly.
